newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr back from brink, but far from safe.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr back from brink, but far from safe.

text.p: The Australian dollar was back from the brink of US$0.7550 support at midday having eked out slight gains in a choppy morning's trade.

It began to edge higher after the Reserve Bank kept silent at its morning operation reflecting just how tense the market is about the risk of another rate cut. A sizeable buy order on AUD/yen kept the rally rolling and took it as high as US$0.7602.

But fresh sales from U.S. and Japanese sources capped it and dealers saw no relief from the downtrend while under US$0.7610. A noteable feature was the Canadian dollar which slid on early signs of a poor election showing by the Liberal government.
By 12.15 am (0215 GMT) the local currency had inched up to US$0.7590/95 from an early US$0.7572/77 and Monday's late US$0.7580/85 but was short of the US$0.7610 top hit offshore.

Bulls were somewhat encouraged by the amount of support at US$0.7550, which marks the year low from February and is viewed as a major chart level. But most conceded the omens for a sustained rally were not good as short term money market rates here moved further beneath those enjoyed by the US$.
Such was the market uncertainty over RBA policy and this being the day of the bank's board meeting, that some feared it might move this morning despite having cut only a fortnight ago.
Most analysts felt an easing this week would smack of panic and expected the bank to absorb at least another month of data before deciding if another was warranted.
That would not stop the market from fearing the worst at Wednesday's morning operation or later in the week if tomorrow's Q1 GDP data were as weak as some expect.

Median forecasts are for a quarterly rise of 0.8 percent which would still see annual growth slow sharply to 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent in Q4. However, estimates range as low as 0.25 percent which would give yr-yr growth of just 1.75 percent.
Anything like the latter will see market rates ease further.

on the crosses the local dollar seesawed on the yen as an early buy order lifted it 1/2 yen to 88.80 only for most of the gains to be wiped out by a retreat in US$/yen. It stood at 88.31/41 by midday from 88.20/30 late Monday.
Dealers said the latter was upset by rumours, later denied, that Finance Ministry forex guru Eisuke Sakakibara had mentioned 103 yen as a suitable level for the dollar.
But both dollars took comfort in comments from the MOF and Bank of Japan that the present low settings of Japanese interest rates were necessary to ensure economic recovery.
The Canadian dollar whipsawed as the poll results flowed.

It dived at first as early results from the election suggested the ruling Liberal Party could be returned with only a minority or even lose power. But it recouped all the losses and more after the national television network projected the Liberals would in fact maintain a majority.

The Canadian dollar fell 3/4 cent to C$1.3830/40 per US$ in early trade but by the midsession was up at C$1.3722/32. Similarly, the A$ was back at C$1.0407/21 after rising as high as C$1.0489 at one stage.
In trade weighted terms it was up a shade at 57.9 from 57.8 late Monday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
